fragments.text: Target approved scope: **16 October 2026**. First buyer: a US small retailer or maker selling physical goods in **USD** through an owned branded online store.

Stall replaces the online-store job sold by **Shopify, Squarespace Commerce, BigCommerce and WooCommerce**: build and merchandise a store, attract and convert shoppers, take payment, deliver orders, support returns and account for the result. **Medusa, Saleor and Fourthwall** are additional switching/extension reference points. This is the product being built towards, not a description of the current release. No homepage, UI or running behavior changes are authorized by this document round.

The core records are stores/themes/pages, collections/products/variants/media/custom fields, stock modes/store-managed quantities/stock-provider mappings/holds, carts/quotes, customers/consent/storefront event preferences, promotions/gift balances, tax/delivery quotes, orders/payments, shipments/returns/exchanges/refunds, messages, channel listings, accounting postings and attributable work history.
Every record has an explicit store, identity, revision/state
and permission boundary appropriate to its job.
Historical imports retain provenance and never become current payment or stock authority.

A single switching journey runs from migration and domain cutover through catalog discovery, checkout, fulfillment, service, return and reconciled books. The clauses specify buyer behavior and the public-door evidence needed to call it complete. Provider test environments/network-edge fakes establish local logic only; live account, domain, carrier, wallet-device and hosted delivery acceptance must be recorded separately. Fixtures are test-only; production has no invented stock, orders, provider success or fallback service.
| Category | Ecommerce platforms (online storefronts) |
| Incumbents a buyer switches from | Shopify, Squarespace Commerce, BigCommerce, WooCommerce, Medusa, Saleor, Fourthwall |
| First buyer | A US small retailer or maker selling physical goods in USD through an owned branded online store |

**HTTP-001 — Real installed and published HTTP surfaces.** The emitted Worker serves health, real assets, the installed Lobby, shop documents and genuine HTTP/document 404s. The independent marketing homepage, /run and /docs remain the Markdown-derived run site; its Run actions lead to /run. The RER operations contract in SEED-COMMAND-CONTRACT.md remains binding. Build and deploy never run tests.

**Acceptance evidence:** Build and serve the emitted Worker; GET /health, /, /shop and built assets, then unknown document/API paths. Verify successful responses and real 404 status codes; build the run site and follow its public links.

**DEMO-001 — Hosted demo shop that sends nothing.** The homepage's "Try the demo" link opens a hosted demo of the current release (https://demo.run-stall.com/), deployed from this repository's main branch with `rer deploy --demo`. The production demo keeps its real human (Turnstile) check; hosted automated sample-shop acceptance uses a separately admitted hosted test host with test keys at the same SHA. The production start page alone never counts as sample-shop proof. It holds a lived-in sample US shop seeded once after its owner exists: catalog and stock, weeks of orders in every state, a refund awaiting a person's approval, product drafts, an agent credential and the audit trail. A visitor can buy from the public shop and approve the desk's prepared shipment and refund drafts; payment, stock and mail run against the demo's own simulated Stripe and Pier and Base demo mode, so no request reaches a real provider and no mail is delivered. Demo data and simulated providers exist only under demo mode: a production build or deploy refuses `RER_DEMO`, and an ordinary installation starts with empty real business state.

**Acceptance evidence:** Follow the built homepage's Try the demo link to the production entry, verify a 200 response and see the real human (Turnstile) check. Then, on the separately admitted hosted test host with test keys at the same SHA, verify the sample shop, buy from the public shop, approve the prepared refund and a packed order's shipment, and invite a teammate; verify the order is paid and reserved, the refund and dispatch succeed against the simulated providers, and no outbound provider request or mail leaves. Attempt a production build and deploy with `RER_DEMO=1` and verify refusal; start a fresh installation and verify it holds no demo record.

**STORE-001 — Merchant themes, page builder and custom domain.** A merchant chooses a starter theme from a theme library, duplicates it and edits logo, colors, typography, navigation, reusable sections and responsive page templates. An unpublished theme or revision is previewable through a staff preview link; the merchant publishes, switches or rolls back themes without losing pages, menus, collections, products or orders, because content and catalog are stored independently of any theme. The complete theme source and assets export as a documented archive and re-import into the same or another store, with validation that names unsupported or missing sections instead of silently dropping them. A storefront password hides the shop before launch or during migration staging while staff preview keeps working. The merchant connects an owned domain with verified DNS, TLS and canonical redirects. Published themes serve resized, cached images, and the reference theme is measured against Google's "good" Core Web Vitals thresholds at phone width rather than assumed fast.

**Acceptance evidence:** In the merchant desk pick a starter theme from the library, create a reusable hero/product section, preview it on desktop and phone, and publish to a verified test domain. Switch to a second library theme and back, confirm every page, menu, collection, product link and order survives, and roll back a revision. Export the theme source and assets, re-import them into an empty store and compare the rendered pages; import a damaged archive and verify a named refusal. Enable the storefront password and confirm public pages, sitemap and feeds are withheld while staff preview works. Follow HTTPS and www/canonical redirects, and record a Core Web Vitals run of the reference theme at 390 pixels.

**STORE-002 — Navigation, collections and product discovery.** Shoppers browse menus, manual or rule-based collections and category landing pages, search product names/SKUs/attributes, and filter/sort by price, availability, variant attributes and collection. Results, counts, empty states and shareable URLs agree with published, sellable catalog data; unpublished products stay private. Search offers predictive suggestions as the shopper types, and merchants tune it with synonyms (for example "tee" and "t-shirt"), boosted or pinned products for a query, and a search report of top queries and queries with no results.

Current discovery semantics: `/shop` is the browse and search page and its address holds the whole view (`q`, `collection`, `category`, `tag`, `attr.<name>`, `option.<name>`, `min`, `max`, `available`, `sort`, `page`). Results are the published products Pier lists as sellable, 24 per page, with facet counts that apply every other filter; options, price and in-stock are matched on one variant together. A category or collection page is that address with a collection title and description. Search matches words and word prefixes in names, SKUs (including variants'), categories, tags, attributes, variant options and descriptions, widened by synonym groups (terms stored lowercased without punctuation); a pinned product leads its query and still obeys filters, and a boosted product leads other matches. Suggestions start at two characters and never include a product that is not public. The report keeps only normalized query text with counts, never a person, session or address, for up to 5,000 different queries. Menus have two levels and leave out destinations that are not published. Collections, menus, synonyms and pins are changed only by a signed-in owner or administrator, never an agent. ANALYTICS-001 inherits consented session analytics, STORE-001 theme presentation, and STORE-003 search-engine visibility (sitemaps and structured data).

**Acceptance evidence:** Publish a varied catalog, navigate collections, search and combine filters on desktop and phone. Change publication and stock, refresh the public results, and verify matching counts, saved URLs and a useful no-results state. Add a synonym and a pinned product for a query and verify both change results; search a term with no results and find it in the search report.

**STORE-003 — Content, blog, contact, newsletter and search visibility.** Merchants manage content pages, blog posts, policies, menus, product/collection SEO titles and descriptions, image alt text, canonical URLs, sitemap, robots policy, social previews, structured product data and permanent redirects. Draft/scheduled content is previewable and changes retain publication history. Moving a product URL preserves discovery through redirects. Every theme includes a contact page whose form delivers each submission, with optional order number, to the store's notification email (reply-to set to the shopper) and to a desk inbox, or to a connected help desk such as sibling [HappyToHelp](https://github.com/just-every/run-happytohelp); Cloudflare Turnstile, a honeypot and per-sender rate limits hold spam for review instead of silently dropping it. A newsletter signup block (footer, page section or popup) records an explicit marketing opt-in under CUSTOMER-002 with source, form, page and timestamp, optionally confirmed by double opt-in, and propagates the subscriber to Mango, Klaviyo or Mailchimp through MARKET-001 without duplicating an existing contact.

**Acceptance evidence:** Create and schedule a blog post and policy page through the desk, publish a product with SEO metadata, fetch its rendered HTML/sitemap, and rename its slug. Verify old URLs redirect once and unpublished content is absent from public search and feeds. Submit the contact form and confirm it reaches the merchant email with the shopper as reply-to and appears in the desk inbox; submit scripted spam and verify it is held, not delivered or lost. Sign up through the footer, confirm the subscriber has source, page and timestamp, and verify the same consented subscriber appears once in Mango and in a Klaviyo or Mailchimp test account; repeat the signup and verify no duplicate.
**MOBILE-001 — Accessible mobile shopping and merchant work.** The complete catalog-to-receipt, account, return and merchant order workflows work at 390 and 1440 pixels
with keyboard and screen-reader labels, visible focus, sufficient contrast and actionable errors.
WCAG 2.2 AA is the target.
Human-readable state and freshness distinguish unavailable data from zero stock or success; failed actions retain input and prevent duplicate submission.

**Acceptance evidence:** Use the built storefront and desk at both widths to buy variants, recover a validation failure, read order status, request a return and process it. Complete the same essential controls by keyboard and inspect accessible names and focus after dialogs/errors.
Run an automated WCAG 2.2 AA scan, including its color-contrast rule, on each storefront, checkout, account and desk page at both widths and verify no violations.

**MOBILE-002 — Native merchant apps and timely order attention.** iOS and Android merchant apps provide secure sign-in, order/customer lookup, product/photo edits, stock visibility, barcode-assisted picking, fulfillment including the pickup and local-delivery steps (SHIP-007), returns and approval notifications under the same role checks as the web desk. Offline drafts show stale data and reconcile conflicts before effects; device revocation removes authority and lock-screen notices avoid customer details.

**Acceptance evidence:** On each platform receive a new-order notification, scan a purchased SKU, prepare fulfillment offline, change the order elsewhere, and reconnect. Verify the conflict requires fresh approval. Edit a product's title and price and add a photo taken with the device camera, and verify the change goes through the same revision approval and appears on the storefront with the photo served from owned storage. Mark a pickup order ready and picked up from the app (SHIP-007) and verify one notice and one dispatch. Revoke the device and confirm private reads and actions fail.

**CATALOG-001 — Products, variants and media.** The desk maintains products, handles, SKUs, variant options/combinations, USD prices and compare-at prices, cost basis, taxable categories, categories/tags/attributes, collections, image galleries and video/alt text. Merchants define typed custom fields (metafields such as size charts, care instructions or ingredients) that themes render on product pages and that imports and exports carry. Products can ask the shopper for personalization (engraving or monogram text with a character limit, a choice list, or a file upload with type and size limits), optionally with a USD price add-on; it is validated before add to cart and carried to the cart, checkout review, order, packing slip, confirmation email and exports, and uploaded files are stored privately under erasure (ERASURE-001). Each variant has independent stock mode and availability (STOCK-001/003), shipping weight/dimensions, and customs description, HS tariff code and country of origin for international labels (SHIP-002). Draft, scheduled, published and archived states preserve historical purchased descriptions/prices and expose only approved current listings.

Current metadata semantics: optional cost is a nonnegative integer number of USD cents; weight is positive whole grams and dimensions are positive whole millimeters (all three together). HS codes accept 6, 8 or 10 digits and origin accepts two uppercase letters; these format checks make no tax, customs or country-validity verification claim. Up to 20 uniquely keyed custom fields carry a text, finite number or boolean value. Omitted details preserve the prior prepared/current facts; an explicit empty details object clears them. Legacy orders without a description snapshot remain unknown rather than borrowing the current listing.

Current listing semantics: A product's page is `/shop/<handle>` (lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens), unique across current and prepared revisions and derived from the SKU when blank. A product has up to three options and up to 100 variants, one per combination. Each variant has its own SKU, unique across products, and may override price, compare-at price, cost, weight, dimensions, HS code, country of origin, customs description and image; a compare-at price must exceed the price it accompanies. Publication requires every variant on sale to be an active Pier item, and each variant's availability is its own Pier item's. Independent stock modes other than Pier-tracked (untracked, store-managed and alternate connectors) are inherited by STOCK-001 and STOCK-003. Images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) and videos (MP4, WebM) are typed by their content, kept in Stall's database at up to 700 KB each with required alt text, and public only while a published listing references them. Categories (10), tags (30) and attributes (30) are plain text; collections are STORE-002's records, which list a product by SKU or match it by these values. Personalization has up to five fields: text up to 500 characters without control characters, a choice list that accepts only its choices, or a file field that accepts only its selected types (PNG, JPG, PDF), judged by content, up to its limit (at most 700 KB). An add-on price is charged per unit and only the reviewed price is accepted. An uploaded file is private to owners and administrators, attaches to one order, is deleted by customer erasure (ERASURE-001) and, if no order claims it, after 24 hours. A listing is a draft until approved, scheduled while approved with a future publish time, published afterwards and archived when withdrawn; only published listings are public and every order keeps its purchased name, description, variant, personalization and price. When payment is verified Stall makes one plain-text confirmation attempt and records whether it was sent; durable outbox, delivery and bounce evidence and branded templates are inherited by MAIL-001, and carrier packing-slip templates by SHIP-002. The packing slip is a staff-only printable page. Imports carry listing fields through the Stall Details JSON (CATALOG-002 inherits the richer file formats).

**Acceptance evidence:** Create a product with size/color variants, multiple images, cost, weight, tax category, HS code, country of origin and a size-chart custom field; publish an approved revision and verify the custom field renders on the product page. Buy one variant, change its current price and archive another; verify gallery/selection and immutable order snapshots through public product and order views. Add an engraving field (20 characters, +$5) and an artwork upload to a product, refuse over-length text and a disallowed file type, buy with valid personalization and verify it with the add-on price on the cart, order, packing slip and confirmation email.

**CATALOG-002 — Bulk catalog operations and portable files.** Merchants import, export and bulk-edit products/variants, collections, prices, publication, tax settings, stock mode, weight, dimensions, HS codes, countries of origin and custom fields. A dry run shows creations, changes, conflicts and rejected rows before an exact reviewed apply; jobs resume without duplicates and offer undo only where later native edits or orders will be preserved. Original source custody and row-level outcomes remain inspectable.
*Cites:* CATALOG-001 and SHIP-004.

Current bulk semantics: the native catalog CSV uses Kind, ID and Value columns for complete product and collection records; the legacy Shopify subset keeps its draft-only behavior. The complete grid reuses native product and variant editors. Native apply is an explicit exact-reviewed human catalog approval, replacing any prepared revision; publication and scheduling require current active Pier items for every live variant and the same listing checks as individual approval. Tax categories and customs fields remain merchant-authored facts, not provider verification. Pier-tracked is the currently supported stock mode; STOCK-001 and STOCK-003 retain other stock authorities and CATALOG-003 retains quantity adjustments. Shipping-profile assignments keep their separate SHIP-004 reviewed grid and catalog CSV, remain unchanged by catalog edits and protect products or variants that undo would otherwise remove. Current local authority is checked on every apply, resume, export and undo. Complete before-images, original source bytes and per-row outcomes travel with the journal; undo preserves later native work, purchased variants and retained collection references without changing orders or provider stock.

**Acceptance evidence:** Upload a mixed valid/invalid catalog file, inspect a read-only preview, apply the reviewed rows, resume an interrupted batch, export them and undo untouched changes. Edit/purchase an imported SKU first and verify undo reports the protected row rather than overwriting it.

**CATALOG-003 — Bulk quantity adjustments through the stock authority.** Merchants bulk-edit on-hand quantities per location. Quantity changes from the bulk grid or an inventory CSV are written to each variant's stock authority (STOCK-001/003) with Stall and provider references recorded together. This clause inherits STOCK-001 and STOCK-003. The Pier-connected leg requires Pier's future scoped stock-adjustment command: Stall's current Pier key admits only order.create, order.channelPayment and dispatch.create and cannot call an on-hand adjustment command today. The store-managed leg requires STOCK-003's local stock authority.

**Acceptance evidence:** Bulk-edit on-hand quantities in the grid and by an inventory CSV, once with store-managed stock and once with Pier connected, and verify each change appears once in the stock authority's history with a matching reference.

**STOCK-001 — Live availability through Pier or another stock system.** Stall displays variant-level sellable availability from each variant's stock authority and reserves against the selected location/fulfillment policy. A variant may be untracked or use store-managed quantities with no stock system at all (STOCK-003); Pier is an optional first-class adapter, and a documented connector lets a merchant retain another stock system. Stall owns storefront merchandising and retail order experience; Pier owns the Cin7/inFlow-style inventory, purchasing and wholesale order system. Backorder/preorder rules, lead times, safety stock and stale-provider behavior are visible before purchase. Changes that start in Stall (on-hand adjustments from the product editor, bulk editor or inventory CSV, sale reservations, cancellation releases and accepted restocks from RETURN-002) are written to the connected stock system with Stall's and the provider's references recorded together; changes that start in the stock system (receipts, counts, transfers) flow back to availability. Neither side becomes a second warehouse ledger. Before this capability ships new provider work, it inherits INTEGRATION-001: installation-local secret custody, least privilege, mapping/data-boundary previews, durable original intent/correlation/attempt/outcome and recovery without replacement uncertain effects.

**Acceptance evidence:** Connect Pier, publish variants across two locations, make an external stock change and verify public availability. Adjust a variant's on-hand quantity from the product editor, the bulk editor and an inventory CSV and verify each adjustment lands once in Pier with matching references. Repeat both via the documented alternate adapter; test backorder refusal/allowed lead time, stale stock and duplicate reservation events with matching stock-provider references. Set a safety stock of 2 on a variant with 5 on hand and verify the storefront sells exactly 3 before showing it sold out.

**STOCK-002 — Expiring checkout holds and stock race resolution.** Checkout rechecks availability and creates a bounded stock hold before payment commitment. Holds expire or release after abandonment, failed payment and cancellation; a verified payment converts the same hold into a reservation once. Late payment or shortfall remains an explicit exception with feasible fulfillment, shopper-approved substitution or reconciled cancellation/refund rather than silently overselling.

**Acceptance evidence:** Two shoppers attempt the last unit through checkout. Expire one hold and fail another payment; verify releases. Deliver late/duplicate success and lose a reservation response; confirm one reservation or a visible paid-shortfall case resolved by the shopper-approved outcome. While the first shopper's hold is live, verify the second shopper is told the last unit is held, with the hold's remaining time, and cannot pay for it, and that it becomes buyable again as soon as the hold expires or that payment fails.

**STOCK-003 — Store-managed quantities and untracked items without a stock system.** Each variant has a stock mode: untracked (made-to-order or unlimited, optionally with a production lead time shown before purchase), store-managed quantities kept by Stall per store location, or a connected stock system (STOCK-001). With no stock system connected, a merchant can sell, hold, reserve and fulfill untracked and store-managed variants; adjust on-hand counts with a reason (received, correction, damaged, cycle count) from the product editor, the bulk editor or an inventory CSV; see on-hand, committed and available quantities per location with adjustment history; and choose per variant whether to continue selling when out of stock. Store-managed counts are the retail quantities a Shopify-class store keeps, not purchasing, transfers or wholesale, which remain Pier's job. Connecting Pier or another stock system later moves opening balances through a reviewed handoff, after which that system is authoritative and Stall's counts become read-through. Before this capability ships new provider work, it inherits INTEGRATION-001: installation-local secret custody, least privilege, mapping/data-boundary previews, durable original intent/correlation/attempt/outcome and recovery without replacement uncertain effects.

**Acceptance evidence:** With no stock system connected, sell and manually fulfill (ORDER-002) a made-to-order untracked variant and a store-managed variant; verify committed and on-hand counts and that the last unit cannot be oversold unless continue-selling is on. Adjust on-hand counts from the editor, bulk editor and CSV with reasons and inspect the adjustment history. Connect Pier, review and apply the opening-balance handoff, and verify later adjustments are written through Pier with matching references while Stall keeps no independent count.

**CART-001 — Persistent cart and guest or account checkout.** Shoppers add/remove variants, change quantities, retain a cart across refresh/sign-in, and check out as guests or account holders. Native shopping/checkout steps collect US addresses, and international addresses in the destination's format for zones the merchant serves (SHIP-001), plus contact, selected delivery method, an optional order note and a gift message with an optional gift receipt that hides prices. They show reviewed USD item, discount, gift-card, shipping, tax and final payable totals before committing payment. Material changes require review again; stock, price and address errors preserve the basket. Saved carts never grant access to another customer. Order notes and gift messages appear on the order, packing slip and confirmation. Merchants can add their own checkout fields (for example "How did you hear about us?", a preferred delivery date or a gift-wrap choice) as required or optional text, choice or date inputs; answers are stored on the order and appear in the order desk, exports and reports (ANALYTICS-001). Current native HTTP cart defaults pending ct approval: a private HttpOnly guest capability or an independently verified account owns each cart. Sign-in handoff is explicit and allowed only to the same verified mailbox, with no foreign-cart or old guest-cookie access afterward. Current Stripe checkout serves US delivery; a Canadian address can be saved but is refused before payment without losing the basket. Review binds the cart revision, published lines, delivery, current checkout questions and exact USD totals. Required merchant questions apply to every existing public Stripe checkout door. Once a checkout starts, immutable original intent and its idempotency identity survive lost replies and later catalog changes; a restored cart carries history without spending authority and needs a fresh copy/review. Shopper note/gift/answer snapshots are separate from internal staff notes and are erased with customer contact. Gift redemption and provider tax are unavailable, labelled explicitly rather than inferred from a zero applied amount.

**Acceptance evidence:** Build a multi-variant cart, reload and sign in, choose a US address and delivery method, add an order note and gift message, apply a discount/gift card and review exact totals. Change price or availability concurrently and verify a fresh review; repeat as a guest, as a different account and with a Canadian address. Verify the note and gift message on the order and packing slip and a gift receipt without prices. Add a required "How did you hear about us?" choice field, verify checkout refuses to continue without it, and find the answer on the order, in the order export and in a report grouped by answer.

**PAY-001 — US dollar cards, wallets, PayPal, pay-later and manual payments.** The merchant connects their own Stripe and PayPal accounts. Checkout supports USD cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay and Link/Shop-style accelerated wallet checkout, PayPal and PayPal Pay Later, and buy-now-pay-later through Stripe's Klarna, Affirm and Afterpay methods, using supported provider adapters and eligibility checks. Pay-later options appear only within each provider's current order-amount and shopper-country eligibility, show the provider's installment terms, and can be advertised on product and cart pages through provider messaging; the merchant is paid by the provider and refunds return through the same method. Merchants can also offer manual methods (bank transfer, cash on delivery, pay at pickup) whose orders stay pending payment until staff record receipt; fulfilling an unpaid manual order requires an explicit merchant setting. Eligible payment choices and unsupported devices are honestly presented; customer payment credentials stay with the processor and wallet. Refunds and receipts retain original method/currency references. Before this capability ships new provider work, it inherits INTEGRATION-001: installation-local secret custody, least privilege, mapping/data-boundary previews, durable original intent/correlation/attempt/outcome and recovery without replacement uncertain effects.

**Acceptance evidence:** Complete USD purchases with a card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Link and PayPal through their supported test/eligible-device doors; inspect provider IDs, amount/currency, failure/cancel paths and a same-method refund. Complete a test-mode Klarna, Affirm, Afterpay and PayPal Pay Later purchase and refund each; verify every pay-later option is withheld, with an explanation, below and above its eligibility range. Verify provider pay-later messaging appears on the product and cart pages with installments computed from the current price, updates when the cart changes, and disappears outside eligibility. Place bank-transfer and pay-at-pickup orders and verify they stay unpaid and unfulfillable until staff record payment. A live provider/device acceptance run is required before claiming production wallet readiness.

**PAY-002 — Authorization, capture, cancellation and disputes.** Merchants choose supported immediate capture or authorize-then-capture rules, see pending/authorized/captured/failed/expired/canceled states, and reconcile asynchronous payments, voids, disputes, chargebacks and provider fees. No fulfillment occurs on an unverified browser return or mere authorization. Expired authorization and a disputed payment create accountable staff work. For a dispute the desk assembles evidence (order and receipt, policies, customer communications, carrier tracking and delivery scans) into the processor's evidence fields; staff review and submit it to Stripe or PayPal before the response deadline, and the outcome and dispute fees reconcile to the order. Permitted captures/refunds bind current order and provider state. Before this capability ships new provider work, it inherits INTEGRATION-001: installation-local secret custody, least privilege, mapping/data-boundary previews, durable original intent/correlation/attempt/outcome and recovery without replacement uncertain effects.

**Acceptance evidence:** Authorize an order without capture, attempt fulfillment, capture once, then process a failed/expired authorization, asynchronous success and dispute event. Assemble and submit evidence for a test dispute on Stripe and PayPal, and verify the processor received it and the won/lost outcome and fee reconcile. Duplicate/out-of-order callbacks must preserve actual processor state, correct balance and a visible owner action.

**PAY-003 — Verified payment and duplicate-safe paid reservation.** A signed payment event must match its raw body, timestamp, event identity, original order/session, exact-cent amount and currency, and canonical processor state before an order is treated as paid. Repeated delivery and lost stock responses reconcile to the same paid order and Pier reservation. A paid shortfall remains recorded; a browser success page alone proves nothing. Changed reuse of an idempotency identity is refused.

**Acceptance evidence:** Through public checkout and the signed webhook send unpaid, stale, wrongly signed, changed-total and duplicate events; lose the Pier response after its commit, then reconcile. Inspect one payment/order/reservation and durable paid-before-reservation history.

**PROMO-001 — Discounts, automatic promotions and controlled budgets.** Merchants create each Shopify-class discount type as either a code or an automatic discount: percentage or fixed amount off selected products, variants or collections; percentage or fixed amount off the order subtotal; Buy X get Y (buy a quantity of, or spend an amount on, qualifying items and get specified items free or at a percentage/amount off, with a per-order use limit, including buy-one-get-one); and free shipping with a minimum subtotal or quantity, eligible zones/countries and an optional maximum rate. Each has date windows, customer eligibility/segments, minimums, per-customer/total usage, combination rules across product, order and shipping discounts, and budgets. Merchants can bulk-generate unique single-use codes for influencers or affiliates, export them and see redemption per code. Checkout explains applied/refused promotions, allocates discounts to lines for tax and refunds, records the chosen rule revision and emits qualification/redemption/reversal events. Concurrent baskets cannot exceed a shared cap; refund/cancellation treatment is explicit.

Approved policy: CT approved the free-shipping-code default on 22 October: owner and administrator management; reserved and used allocations consume caps; restored rules require fresh activation. The same current-authority and exact-cents boundary governs the added native rules. An unpaid reservation is released only after the provider confirms that its checkout expired or never existed; paid use and refunds retain consumption. Product discounts apply before order discounts, then shipping, with both rules consenting to each combination. Fixed product and order amounts apply once to the selected subtotal; fixed Buy X get Y amounts apply to each reward unit. Reward units never qualify themselves and cheapest eligible reward units are selected first. Each order retains the chosen revisions, exact line allocations and original tax references. These semantics do not waive the original acceptance journey or the shared TAX-001 calculation boundary. End-to-end cancellation remains unproved because the supported Pier connection cannot cancel its reserved order; no stock release or canceled-order success is inferred.

**Acceptance evidence:** Configure each type once as a code and once as an automatic discount: amount and percentage off a product and a collection, amount off the order, a buy-one-get-one and a spend-$X Buy X get Y, and free shipping over $50. Build qualifying and non-qualifying baskets and verify the reviewed checkout totals, line allocations and tax to the cent. Exercise combination rules, race the last redemption of a capped code, generate a batch of unique single-use codes and refuse a second use of one, cancel one order and partially refund another. Reconcile campaign usage, budget and exact order/tax totals from the merchant report and emitted events.

**PROMO-002 — Gift cards and stored redemption balances.** Merchants sell or issue gift cards, deliver secure codes, inspect a balance ledger and redeem partially across orders alongside another method. Concurrent redemption, cancellation and refund preserve value exactly once; issuance, expiry restrictions and cash-out handling follow the configured US jurisdiction/policy and are explicit to the shopper. Gift cards sold to shoppers follow the federal CARD Act (no expiry earlier than five years after issue or last load, no dormancy or inactivity fee in the first twelve months) unless the store's state is stricter, and the store's state sets cash-out rules, such as California's requirement to pay balances under $10 in cash on request; free promotional cards are labeled as promotional with their own terms. Staff can also issue store credit to a customer outside any return (goodwill, loyalty or a price adjustment) with a USD amount, reason and optional expiry; it shows in the customer's account and applies at checkout like a balance, alone or alongside another method, and return-resolution credit (RETURN-002) uses the same ledger of issue, use, expiry and staff adjustment. Exported balances and migrated cards reconcile without revealing full codes to unauthorized staff.

**Acceptance evidence:** Issue a USD gift card, deliver and redeem it partly, race its remaining balance in two checkouts, and cancel/refund the winning order. Inspect the balance ledger, shopper receipt, staff permissions and reconciled migrated opening balance. Try to give a sold card a two-year expiry and verify refusal under the five-year rule, while a promotional card may carry it. With a California store, request cash-out of a $7.50 remaining balance and verify a recorded payout zeroes the ledger, and verify a $15.00 balance is refused cash-out. Issue $20.00 goodwill store credit to a customer with no return, sign in as that customer, see it in the account and apply $12.00 of it at checkout alongside a card; verify the ledger shows $8.00 remaining. Sell a $50.00 gift card through storefront checkout, verify the buyer receives its code by email once payment is verified, and redeem it at checkout on a later order.

Checkout shows jurisdictional tax before payment; order records preserve the calculation reference and refunds reverse the correct tax. Provider outage or incomplete configuration blocks a taxed sale with a useful explanation, rather than inventing a zero rate. A sales-tax liability report shows, for any filing period, a state overview (gross, taxable, non-taxable and exempt sales, shipping, tax collected, refunds and adjustments, with marketplace-facilitated channel sales separated), then county, city and special-district breakdowns, then the contributing transactions; each level exports as CSV and drills to orders and provider calculation/transaction references, and refunds land in the period they occur. A nexus view tracks per-state sales and transaction counts against the merchant's configured economic-nexus thresholds and warns before one is crossed. Registration and filing stay with the merchant, adviser or a filing service such as Avalara Returns or TaxJar AutoFile, fed by these exports.

Current implementation semantic: the owner-only HTTP preview door sends complete US destination and ship-from addresses, explicit product tax codes, quantity-extended line amounts and already-discounted shipping to the connected Stripe test account after explicit data-boundary consent. Amounts are exclusive USD integer cents; provider totals and breakdown must reconcile. Active head-office settings, a default tax code and an observed destination-state registration are required. A preview is never a payment, registration, filing or tax transaction. The durable journal keeps no street address; an uncertain calculation is recovered only by retrieving its original reference and matching the full original inputs and line metadata, never by a replacement POST. Restored previews are observation-only and require the original provider calculation. The owner-only consent and restore boundary is approved with riders (ct 25 October 2026). The preview does not enable taxed checkout or substitute for the remaining acceptance journey.

It is clearly labelled preview-only. No local jurisdiction name or zero rate is invented from incomplete provider evidence. The complete TAX-001 checkout, exemption, order-reference, refund, reporting, CSV, nexus-warning and live test-mode receipt obligations remain unchanged. Pickup and local-delivery orders are completed through SHIP-007, never through a carrier label. Each location has a daily handling cutoff, handling days and a business-day and holiday calendar; the delivery date or range promised at checkout is computed from them and the service's transit time, is shown on the product page and in checkout, and the paid order keeps the promise it was sold under. Split-source orders show combined charges and feasible dates. Local currencies and regional storefronts are EXPAND-001. **SHIP-004 — Shipping profiles for specific products.** Merchants group products or variants into shipping profiles: a general profile every product starts in, plus custom profiles (at least the 99 Shopify allows) for items such as oversized, fragile, free-shipping or local-only goods. Each profile has its own ship-from locations, zones, rates (free, flat, weight- or price-based, carrier-calculated, with optional surcharge or handling fee) and allowed services, and can be pickup-only or local-delivery-only. Products and variants are assigned to a profile in the product editor, the bulk editor and catalog CSV (CATALOG-001/002), and Shopify shipping profiles map across in migration (MIGRATE-001). For a cart that spans profiles, each offered service is priced as the sum of each profile's rate for its own items in that service; a service is offered only when every profile in the cart allows it; a pickup-only or local-delivery-only item removes shipped services for the order and says which item caused it. A variant whose profile does not serve the destination is refused before payment, naming the line and keeping the rest of the basket. Each quote records the profile revisions it used; editing a profile or reassigning a product invalidates open quotes, and the paid order keeps the profile revision and quoted charge it was sold under.

Current profile semantics: the general profile (`general`, which holds the shop's earlier flat domestic charge as its one `standard` service) and up to 99 custom profiles, each with its own ID, name, ship-from label, ZIP-prefix zones (one to five leading digits; none means every US ZIP), up to 20 services and pickup and local-delivery switches. A service has a code, a name and a rate: free, flat, weight bands (grams, from the variant's weight, else the product's) or price bands (the profile's subtotal including add-ons), plus an optional handling fee once per profile in the basket and a surcharge per item. A rate applies once per profile per basket; a weight or price past the last band means that profile does not offer the service. A product or variant is assigned to a profile by SKU (a variant's own assignment wins over its product's), stored apart from product revisions and effective at once. For a basket, a shipped service is offered only when every profile in it offers that service code, priced as the sum of each profile's rate for its own items; a profile with no shipped service removes shipped services for the basket and the quote names its items; a profile whose zones miss the shopper's ZIP code lists its lines as unserved, and checkout refuses a shipped service before any payment, naming them, while the rest of the basket stays. Pickup and local delivery use the shop's one pickup place and one delivery area (ZIP prefixes, fee, minimum) and are offered when every profile allows them; delivery also needs a ZIP inside the area and the minimum met. Each offered service carries a quote key derived from the destination ZIP, the basket, the used profiles' revisions and the computed charge; checkout with a stale key is refused, and the paid order keeps its service, ZIP, quote key, profile revisions and charge. The ZIP is the one the shopper entered in the shop; Stripe collects the delivery address afterwards (pickup collects none) and Stall does not compare the two. Profiles, places and assignments are changed only by a signed-in owner or administrator, never an agent, are audited, travel in the archive and the records export, and the customer's erasure removes an order's quoted ZIP and quote key. Bulk assignment (the Products grid and a catalog CSV with the headers `SKU,Shipping Profile`) shows every change and applies only the reviewed fingerprint; the catalog CSV is the acceptance's catalog-or-inventory CSV leg, as ct approved on 22 October. Stock-quantity adjustment is CATALOG-003 and STOCK-003. Inherited by later clauses: SHIP-001 (carrier-calculated rates, state zones, per-location pickup and delivery areas, handling cut-offs and promises, address verification), SHIP-002 (labels), SHIP-007 (completing pickup and delivery orders), MIGRATE-001 (mapping Shopify's profiles), CATALOG-002 (the grid and catalog CSV carry the profile column as they widen), CATALOG-003 (the inventory CSV carries the profile column when stock adjustments ship), and every later record kind inherits archive, export, audit and erasure duties.

Repeating a step, a double tap or a stale screen observes the current state and sends no second notice or dispatch. A pickup order not collected within the merchant's pickup window (for example 7 days after ready) becomes a staff task with an optional reminder notice, and staff can cancel and refund it under ORDER-004 with a reason, releasing the set-aside stock. The customer's order view and the merchant's history show each state, who set it and when. Before this capability ships new provider work, it inherits INTEGRATION-001: installation-local secret custody, least privilege, mapping/data-boundary previews, durable original intent/correlation/attempt/outcome and recovery without replacement uncertain effects.

Stored commercial timestamps and exported timestamp fields remain UTC. Order filters combine: status, customer text, item SKU, a placed-date range and overdue work. A date range is the shop zone's calendar days of placement, both ends inclusive; an order is overdue when it is partly shipped and its latest recorded Pier dispatch (payment time when unstamped) is more than 7 × 24 hours old, a derived label that never changes the order. One history per order lists every audited action with actor and time and the provider references the record keeps. Only a signed-in owner or admin saves the zone; members and agent credentials are refused, the save is audited, and any canonical IANA zone may be saved. A calendar day runs from the first instant of that date in the zone to the first instant of the next, 23 or 25 hours across a transition. Clauses that later add local days, times or date windows (SHIP-001, SHIP-007, PROMO-001/002, RETURN-001, FLOW-001, RECOVERY-001, MAIL-001, ANALYTICS-001, TAX-001, ACCOUNT-001) use this zone unless their own text names another, name it where a shopper sees a time, and resolve a repeated local time to its first occurrence and a skipped one to the first instant after the gap. The channel filter (“Online store”, “Manual”) combines with the others; ORDER-005 and CHANNEL-001/002/004 add their channels when they ship. Each note, tag or redaction is an audited action in the order's history. Notes and tags never reach a shopper or an outside party: no storefront, checkout, notice, receipt, packing slip, customer view, provider or connection payload or API event carries them. They are separate from a shopper's order note or gift message (CART-001). Owner exports and archives include them. Customer erasure replaces each note's text on the erased customer's orders with “Erased with customer contact”, keeping note ID, author and time, and removes those orders' tags and manual payment references; a restored archive keeps them erased (ERASURE-001). Text about a customer on another customer's order is not detected. The ORDER-001/ORDER-006 numeric fallback and the existing PENDING_EFFECT refusal are accepted, with policy unchanged. A manual retail order records a sale already paid outside Stall. A signed-in owner/admin or ROLE-001 finance staff member enters published catalog items at current USD prices and positive whole quantities within checkout's limits, plus the customer's email, name and US shipping address and the shop's configured shipping charge. Members and agent credentials are refused, and creation fails if the server's total differs from the total the staff member reviewed. Its payment is staff-recorded: cash, check, bank transfer or other, for exactly the order total in integer cents, with a received date in the shop zone that is not after today and an optional plain-text reference. It is labelled “Payment recorded by staff, not confirmed by a payment provider” wherever it appears and never counts as a PAY-003 verified payment. It records `no_tax_recorded`, and Stall sends no confirmation or receipt. Orders awaiting payment, custom lines, discounts and invoices remain ORDER-005 and PAY-001, which reuse this recorded payment and its label. TAX-001, MAIL-001, ACCOUNT-001, ANALYTICS-001 and ORDER-004 cover manual orders when they ship.

Failed/canceled attempts free their budgets; drafts do not reserve value and are replaced under the order revision. Historical orders without a shipping charge have zero shipping refundable. **AI-004 — Recover failed integration work without invented success.** An agent correlates signed event IDs, immutable order revisions, provider payment/stock/label/mail/channel references and accounting entries to explain missing or contradictory work. It queries the original operation, proposes a scoped correction/replay and verifies resulting totals. Owners approve mappings, material ledger corrections and any irreversible effect; already-approved safe reconciliation can run within a revocable policy. **Acceptance evidence:** Lose a successful processor/stock/label/ledger response and supply an out-of-order event. Inspect the agent's cited diagnosis and proposed correction, approve the material action, and verify one external effect and matched stock/money/ledger totals. Revoke policy during work and confirm it stops before a new effect.

It flags unsupported claims and missing size, material and safety information, previews changes and feed validation, and never fabricates inventory, certifications or customer reviews. Merchant approval publishes the exact revision; measured conversion and margin feedback can inform the next proposal without granting autonomous publication.
